newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News- Oct 18.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News- Oct 18.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The partners in Australia's North-West Shelf project have released plans to invest up to A$6 billion to double the size of the liquefied natural gas project. The move will see a doubling in LNG production to an additional 14.5 million tonnes annually. Page 1.

With a new consumer credit code coming into effect in two weeks, Australia's big four banks estimate the cost of compliance with the new code will cost more than A$50 million. The new laws will force banks, such as National Australia Bank, to withdraw or amend much of their advertising, including posters and brochures, to ensure each item complies with the law. Page 1.

According to the Australian Information Industry Association's annual report released yesterday, Australia's information technology and telecommunications sector grew four times more quickly than gross domestic product in 1995-96, while overall revenue of member companies rose 18 per cent to more than A$29.4 billion and capital investment surged 32 per cent to more than A$5.6 billion. Page 3.

The Federal Government's decision to cut the Research and Development tax concession from 150 per cent to 125 per cent has forced 34 per cent of large and medium-sized Australian companies to consider doing their research and development overseas, accordig to a Deloitte Touche Tomatsu survey, which covered 125 companies, including many of Australia's leading firms. Page 3.

With a decision on an Aboriginal injunction application over work on a power link to MIM Holding Ltd's Ernest Henry copper project due in the Federal Court today, it was revealed last night the north-west Queensland project faces another obstacle, in the form of a A$120 million native title claim. The Mitakoodi Juhnjlar Aboriginal Corporation has informed Ernest Henry that in return for approximately A$120 million as compensation for land use, the group would ensure no native title claim would interfere wth the mine. Page 31.

The Australian Stock Exchange's "natural members" are today expected to vote in favour of its demutualisation, with a yes vote from at least 75 per cent of the 527 individual stockbrokers and 99 broking firms eligible to vote meaning they would receive shares that could ultimately be traded on the ASX. Page 31.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Optus Communications' plan for a A$4.5 billion float by the end of the year has been shattered by a New South Wales Supreme Court ruling. The capital raising plan will most likely be shelved until the court action - involving its pay TV offshoot Optus Vison, the Seven Network Ltd and Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd - is resolved. Last night, Optus said its shareholders would investigate alternative strategies for proceeding with a float. Page 21.

The North West Shelf gas project has announced plans for a A$6 billion expansion to double its liquefied natural gas capacity to meet demand from Japanese customers. The expansion move could see a further A$3 billion added to Australia's annual export earnings. Page 21.

By delaying an announcement of a significant oil discovery in the Timor Sea, BHP has been rebuked by the Australian Stock Exchange. The announcement of the find on the eastern flank of BHP's Laminaria strike was delayed by eight days after the results of drill stem test were known. The ASX was "concerned" by BHP's failure to comply with the stock market listing obligations. Page 21.

With the release of the draft environmental impact statement yesterday, Energy Resources of Australia Ltd's Jabiluka uranium deposit edged closer to a reality. ERA claims the impact statement addresses all pertinent issues regarding environmental concerns Meanwhile, the deposit has already been declared as the company's most significant project to date. Page 23.

Share prices in Queensland 's Metway Bank Ltd defied the trend in the banking sector and soared to up to A$5.00 yesterday, following the Queensland Government's aim to entice shareholders to accept the State's cash offer of A$4.80 to assist with the current mega-bank proposal. Page 22.

Scrap metal recycler Simsmetal Ltd has suffered a one-third drop in pre-tax earnings for the September quarter. Simsmetal has issued a warning, claiming the worse is yet to come, citing declining demand and weaker prices as the catalyst for the A$13.3 milion profit. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The planned partial float of Optus Communications this year is in doubt because of a Supreme Court decision to give Optus' legal dispute with the Seven Network a full court hearing next year. Seven is claiming that other Optus Vision shareholders, Optus ommunications, Continental Cablevision and Publishing and Broadcasting breached a shareholders' agreement. Page 25.

To cater for Japanese demand, the partners in Australia's North-West Shelf liquefied natural gas development have outlined a A$6 billion expansion program which would see the construction of two more LNG trains to supply energy well into the 21st century, nearly doubling the project's size. Page 25.

The Australian Broadcasting Authority has begun inquiries into the dispute between Canadian group CanWest and key shareholders in the Ten Group as shareholders Robert Whyte and Jack Cowin yesterday requisitioned an extraordinary meeting of Ten shareholder to try to force the company to pursue a sharemarket listing. Page 25.

Two leading brokers have downgraded their 1997 net profit forecasts for building products and petroleum group Pioneer International to A$225 million and A$227 million respectively, following an intense petrol price discounting war in Australia and thin whlesale margins in the Singapore oil market. Page 27.

The Australian Shareholders' Association has forcefully suggested to St George Bank that it hold a shareholders' meeting to approve its A$2.65 billion friendly takeover of Advance Bank, after St George managing director Jim Sweeney indicated this week the bank wanted to go ahead with the takeover without a meeting to reduce the chance of National Australia Bank scuttling the deal. Page 27.

Responding to comments by new Assistant Treasurer Rod Kemp that there would be no change to superannuation surcharge collection methods, Association of Superannuation Funds of Australia president Peter Foxton said the Government's method of collecting the 15 per cent surcharge on members' contributions was expensive and difficult to administer. Page 27.
THE AGE

The planned partial float of the A$4.5 billion Optus Communications was placed in jeopardy yesterday when its pay TV offshoot Optus Vision failed to end a legal dispute with shareholder Seven Network in the Supreme Court, after Seven claimed that all of te other Optus Vision shareholders - Optus Communications, Continental Cablevision and Publishing and Broadcasting - have breached Optus Vision's shareholders' agreement. Page C1.

Releasing a discussion paper seeking industry and investor feedback on the quality of the financial information provided in prospectuses yesterday, the Australian Securities Commission issued a warning to investors that they need to read forecasts criticaly and find out if they are based on reasonable assumptions. Page C1.

A meeting of the Coles Myer board today is expected to formally offer directorships to Myer family representative Martin Myer and Brierley Investments Ltd chief executive Paul Collins. The board is also expected to agree to present a united front at the company's annual meeting next month by backing the expanded board of directors, including vice-chairman Solomon Lew. Page C1.

At meetings in Japan this week, partners in the North West gas project lodged a formal proposal for the expansion of liquefied natural gas production with the project's eight Japanese power and utility customers, clearing the way for a A$6 billion expansin of Australia's biggest resources project, involving the addition of two more LNG processing trains. Page C1.

Addressing a New York Conference, Foster's Brewing Group chief executive Ted Kunkel claimed the brewer has close to A$1 billion of assets making a negligible return. Despite the company posting a A$293 million net profit in 1995-96, Kunkel said a review of some law return businesses in the group will occur. Foster's 50 per cent stake in Britain's Inntrepreneur Pub Company could be up for sale after making little contribution to the group's profit. Page C2.

Pressure to cut interest rates has been placed back on the Reserve Bank, with the release of a Dun and Bradstreet quarterly survey which shows the number of businesses raising prices peaked in March last year and has continued to decline since then, reflecting low inflation expectations. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
